content_voiceover: This is third-line and subsequent therapy, and the note at the top is important, any second-line regimen the patient hasn't already received can still be reused here. The preferred column is built around T-cell mediated therapy. CAR T-cell therapy is preferred, and this slide has been annotated to show a real guideline update, lisocabtagene maraleucel is struck through and tisagenlecleucel has been added in its place alongside axicabtagene ciloleucel, both CD19-directed. That's a detail worth knowing for boards, which specific CAR T products are approved shifts as trials mature and labels change, so don't over-anchor on any single product list. Alongside CAR T, bispecific antibody therapy, epcoritamab or glofitamab, is preferred, and importantly these are usable even in patients who progressed after transplant or after CAR T-cell therapy, which matters because that's a group with very few options otherwise. The other recommended column has three distinct mechanisms, lenalidomide plus brentuximab vedotin plus rituximab, loncastuximab tesirine, an antibody-drug conjugate, and selinexor, a nuclear export inhibitor, which is also explicitly usable after transplant or CAR T failure.
keypoints: Unused second-line regimens remain valid options at third-line

keypoint_voiceover: Third-line therapy centers on T-cell engaging approaches, CAR T-cell therapy and bispecific antibodies like epcoritamab and glofitamab, both of which remain options even after a patient has already failed transplant or CAR T. Notice the annotated edit on this slide, liso-cel crossed out and tisagenlecleucel added, a reminder that specific product recommendations evolve. For patients who've exhausted T-cell approaches, loncastuximab tesirine and selinexor are the fallback mechanisms to know.
